scenes.tts: Press a fingertip on the edge of a coin, and hold it still. What keeps telling your brain where that edge is?
scenes.visual: Title card: Two Receptors, One Nerve. A fingertip pressed on the edge of a coin, held still. Question on screen: what keeps reporting the edge?
scenes.narration: Press a fingertip on the edge of a coin, and hold it still. What keeps telling your brain where that edge is?

scenes.tts: Some nerve fibres from that skin fire only while the skin is moving. Then they go quiet.
scenes.visual: A spike raster labelled rapidly adapting (RA): a few ticks as the press begins, none through the hold, a few as the probe lifts. Schematic.
scenes.narration: Some nerve fibres from that skin fire only while the skin is moving. Then they go quiet.

scenes.tts: Others keep firing for as long as you hold. One such class is the slowly adapting type one afferent, or S A one.
scenes.visual: Beside it, a raster labelled SA1: ticks continue through the whole hold. A bar under both rasters marks press, hold and lift.
scenes.caption: Others keep firing for as long as you hold. One such class is the slowly adapting type I afferent, or SA1.
scenes.narration: Others keep firing for as long as you hold. One such class is the slowly adapting type I afferent, or SA1.

scenes.tts: In macaque fingertips, its firing carried the spatial layout of millimetre-scale features, such as raised patterns.
scenes.visual: A fingertip over a strip of raised dots; a grid of SA1 firing mirrors the dot layout. Label: macaque fingertip recordings.
scenes.narration: In macaque fingertips, its firing carried the spatial layout of millimetre-scale features, such as raised patterns.

scenes.tts: Its firing has two parts. First, a fast burst as the press begins. That is the dynamic phase.
scenes.visual: The SA1 raster: the dense burst at onset is boxed and labelled dynamic phase.
scenes.narration: Its firing has two parts. First, a fast burst as the press begins. That is the dynamic phase.

scenes.tts: Then firing through the hold, with irregular gaps between spikes. That is the static phase.
scenes.visual: The rest of the SA1 raster, unevenly spaced ticks through the hold, is boxed and labelled static phase: irregular intervals.
scenes.narration: Then firing through the hold, with irregular gaps between spikes. That is the static phase.

scenes.tts: Now the surprise. The cell that helps make the hold is not a neuron.
scenes.visual: Zoom into the skin below the fingertip. A round cell in the base of the epidermis lights up, with a question mark: not a neuron?
scenes.narration: Now the surprise. The cell that helps make the hold is not a neuron.

scenes.tts: It is the Merkel cell. In mice, it comes from epidermal progenitors, not from neural crest.
scenes.visual: Label: Merkel cell. A lineage arrow from epidermal progenitors to the Merkel cell; a crossed-out arrow from neural crest. Label: mouse lineage tracing.
scenes.narration: It is the Merkel cell. In mice, it comes from epidermal progenitors, not from neural crest.

scenes.tts: In hairy mouse skin, Merkel cells cluster in touch domes beside guard hairs.
scenes.visual: Cross-section: a guard hair, and beside it a raised touch dome holding a cluster of round Merkel cells in its basal layer.
scenes.narration: In hairy mouse skin, Merkel cells cluster in touch domes beside guard hairs.

scenes.tts: An afferent's branched ending makes disc-like contacts on them.
scenes.visual: One axon rises from below and branches into small discs under the Merkel cells. Label: one afferent, usually.
scenes.narration: An afferent's branched ending makes disc-like contacts on them.

scenes.tts: So force can reach this fibre by two routes.
scenes.visual: Two arrows converge on the single axon. Both arrows are still unlabelled.
scenes.narration: So force can reach this fibre by two routes.

scenes.tts: The ending makes its own Piezo two. Even without Merkel cells, it still responds to touch.
scenes.visual: The first arrow is labelled: the ending's own transduction. A small channel icon sits on the disc, labelled: makes Piezo2.
scenes.caption: The ending makes its own Piezo2. Even without Merkel cells, it still responds to touch.
scenes.narration: The ending makes its own Piezo2. Even without Merkel cells, it still responds to touch.

scenes.tts: Or the Merkel cell feels force through its own Piezo two, and passes the signal across a synapse.
scenes.visual: The second arrow is labelled: the Merkel cell, through a synapse. A channel icon on the Merkel cell; small vesicles at its contact with the disc.
scenes.caption: Or the Merkel cell feels force through its own Piezo2, and passes the signal across a synapse.
scenes.narration: Or the Merkel cell feels force through its own Piezo2, and passes the signal across a synapse.

scenes.tts: Predict. One route reports change. One route holds the press. Which would you guess holds the press?
scenes.visual: Both arrows feed one axon. Beside the SA1 raster, two empty tags wait over the dynamic and static boxes. Text: which route makes which phase?
scenes.narration: Predict. One route reports change. One route holds the press. Which would you guess holds the press?

scenes.tts: In mouse touch domes, the ending mainly carries the onset. The Merkel cell mainly holds the press.
scenes.visual: The dynamic box gets the tag: mainly the ending. The static box gets the tag: mainly the Merkel cell. Label: mouse touch domes.
scenes.narration: In mouse touch domes, the ending mainly carries the onset. The Merkel cell mainly holds the press.

scenes.tts: That is the idea for this lesson. The ending mainly feels the change, and the Merkel cell mainly holds the press.
scenes.visual: Idea card, large: The ending feels the change; the Merkel cell holds the press.
scenes.narration: That is the idea for this lesson. The ending mainly feels the change, and the Merkel cell mainly holds the press.

scenes.tts: This is mouse hairy skin. And the word mainly matters. The Merkel cell may help with the onset too.
scenes.visual: The idea card shrinks to a corner. The word mainly is underlined. Label: scope: mouse touch domes.
scenes.narration: This is mouse hairy skin. And the word mainly matters. The Merkel cell may help with the onset too.

scenes.tts: Rat whiskers give a different reading. There, another laboratory argues that Merkel cells drive both phases.
scenes.visual: A whisker follicle appears beside the touch dome, with both raster boxes highlighted. Label: rat whisker reading: both phases.
scenes.narration: Rat whiskers give a different reading. There, another laboratory argues that Merkel cells drive both phases.

scenes.tts: Keep this. Two receptors feed one nerve, and each mainly makes one phase.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: two arrows into one axon, each arrow thicker under one phase. Line: two receptors, one nerve.
scenes.narration: Keep this. Two receptors feed one nerve, and each mainly makes one phase.
